lines.text: Do you know how a traffic light knows you're waiting? Look down. There's a wire hidden in the road.
Cut into the asphalt is a loop of wire, carrying a small electric current. It makes a magnetic field just above the road.
When a car stops on top, its metal changes that field. A detector at the corner notices the change.
The controller adds you to the queue, and gives your direction a green as soon as it safely can.
Bikes have much less metal, so some roads paint a mark showing exactly where to stop. Many junctions also use cameras or radar.
So that light didn't see you. It felt your car.
